title: Meta policies fail as scam ads, deepfakes impersonating Nigerian public figures litter Facebook
key_facts: In mid-April a sponsored video on the Nigeria Daily Report Facebook page used a deepfake of Senator Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, who represents Kogi Central in Nigeria's National Assembly, to promote an investment scheme; she had disclaimed it.
In May a deepfake of Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, promoted an investment scheme; its link led to a phoney site that cloned Channels Television's website.
Deepfakes also used Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (director-general of the World Trade Organization), Tony Elumelu (chairman of UBA), Jim Ovia (group chairman of Zenith Bank) and Aliko Dangote.
Meta confirmed to Premium Times that the ads and deepfake videos violated its policy; the posts stayed up for months and were removed in July after the newspaper asked Meta about them.
Meta said it removed over 159 million scam ads on Facebook last year and took down 10.9 million accounts linked to criminal scam centres.
Reuters reported last year that Meta projected in 2024 that it would earn about 16 billion dollars, about 10 percent of its revenue, from scam and banned-goods ads.
Nurudeen Akewushola, fact-checker at FactCheckHub, says the sheer scale of such ads overwhelms fact-checkers.
quote_evidence: Meta confirmed to PREMIUM TIMES that the ads and deepfake videos violated its policy.
But these posts remained on the platform for months.
why_it_matters_hint: Deepfake investment scams using public figures stayed on Facebook for months, and people lose money to them.
event_date: April to July 2026 (ads and deepfakes); article dated 8 Oct 2026
notes: Article read in full (11,147 characters). Investigation with Meta's own statements. Premium Times' own reporting, not a copy.
